antarcticseaspider: A sea spider, a marine animal with ALMOST NO BODY AT ALL: eight extremely long thin jointed legs radiate out from a body that is nothing more than a NARROW SEGMENTED ROD no thicker than the legs themselves, so the whole animal reads as a star of legs meeting at a stick. A short tubular snout points forward from the front end. Pale straw-yellow, semi-transparent. Absolutely NOT a house spider: no fat rounded abdomen, no fangs, no silk.
beardedseal: A bearded seal LYING FLAT ON ITS BELLY AND FULLY HORIZONTAL, a true seal with a small head on an enormously thick sausage-shaped body. IT CANNOT PROP ITSELF UPRIGHT: its short front flippers lie flat against its sides and its hind flippers trail straight out behind, so the body stays low to the ground along its whole length. Its muzzle carries a DENSE MOUSTACHE OF LONG PALE WHISKERS CURLING INTO TIGHT SPIRALS at the tips. Plain silvery-grey, with only a small hole where each ear is.
collaredlemming: A collared lemming in winter, a small rodent shaped like a rounded pebble, its fur PURE WHITE AND SO LONG AND DENSE THAT ITS EARS ARE COMPLETELY HIDDEN and its legs are almost buried, so the outline is a smooth featureless oval with a blunt face. Tiny black bead eyes, a short blunt muzzle, no visible tail. On each front paw THE TWO MIDDLE CLAWS ARE GREATLY ENLARGED INTO THICK PALE FORKED DIGGING BLADES, far bigger than the rest.
hoodedseal: A hooded seal lying flat, a big silver-grey seal blotched with irregular black patches, ITS MOUTH CLOSED. THE RED BALLOON EMERGES FROM ONE NOSTRIL AND NOT FROM THE MOUTH: a glossy scarlet sac of membrane inflated out of the left nostril and hanging beside the muzzle, about the size of the seal's own head. Above it, over the top of the muzzle between the eyes, sits a swollen inflated black cushion of skin.
longtailedduck: A long-tailed duck drake in side view, and THE TAIL IS THE WHOLE POINT: TWO EXTREMELY LONG NARROW BLACK TAIL FEATHERS EXTEND STRAIGHT OUT BEHIND IT, EACH AS LONG AS THE DUCK'S ENTIRE BODY FROM BILL TO RUMP, held up clear and trailing like two fine whips. Its head and neck are white with a LARGE SMUDGED GREY-BROWN PATCH ON EACH CHEEK, its breast and back blackish-brown, its flanks white, and its short bill dark with a pink band.
ringedseal: A ringed seal lying flat, a SMALL plump seal with a very short rounded cat-like face, small dark eyes, and a SOLID UNBROKEN BODY. Its coat is dark silver-grey MARKED ALL OVER WITH MANY SMALL PALE OVAL BLOTCHES, each a soft light patch with a slightly darker centre, scattered densely over the back and fading to plain silver on the belly. These are markings on the fur only; the animal's body is solid all the way through.
beardeddragon: A bearded dragon standing flat on all fours, a broad flattened sandy-tan lizard with a wide triangular head. Under its chin hangs a LOOSE FLAP OF DARK GREY-BLACK SKIN, puffed out and COVERED IN SHORT STIFF POINTED SCALES standing up like a bed of small thorns - it is SCALY, SPIKY AND DARK, never soft, never pale and never feathery. Rows of similar pointed scales run along each flank. Long tapering tail, short splayed legs.
littlemarianafruitbat: A little Marianas fruit bat, a FLYING FOX whose face is that of a small fox or dog: a LONG POINTED MUZZLE with a black wet nose at the tip, large round dark eyes, and small simple pointed ears. Dense dark chocolate-brown fur with a PALER GOLDEN-BROWN MANTLE over the shoulders and neck. It sits upright with its thin dark leathery wings FOLDED CLOSED FLAT AGAINST ITS SIDES.
mutt: A mixed-breed dog of NO RECOGNISABLE BREED, standing: a plain medium dog of moderate build with a MEDIUM-LENGTH TAPERED MUZZLE and a short coarse coat in a MUDDY UNEVEN MIX of tan and grey-brown, with a few scruffy off-white patches placed ASYMMETRICALLY and in no tidy pattern. One ear flops over, the other half stands. Its outline is slightly awkward and unbalanced. A shelter mongrel, absolutely NOT a collie, NOT a shepherd and NOT any pedigree breed.
pitbull: An American pit bull terrier standing in side view, an ATHLETIC LEAN WIRY medium dog with a deep but NARROW chest and long straight legs, NOT bulky and NOT wide. Its head is broad across the cheeks but its MUZZLE IS MODERATELY LONG AND SQUARE, about a third the length of the whole head, with a clear step up to the forehead. Short glossy fawn coat, a white blaze on the chest, small forward-folded ears, and a long thin tapering tail.
roundislandburrowingboa: A Round Island boa, a slender snake of even thickness lying in ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS UNBROKEN CURVE FROM HEAD TO TAIL TIP, its whole body joined in one piece with nothing detached. Its head is barely wider than its neck, with a pointed snout and small dark eyes. Every scale carries a raised central ridge so the skin looks matte and rough, and it is pale orange-brown mottled with soft darker olive blotches. The tail tapers smoothly to a fine point.
brownrat: A brown rat, a large heavy rodent with a blunt thick snout, small thick rounded ears set close to the head, and a heavy-shouldered body. ITS TAIL IS A SMOOTH UNIFORM PINK-GREY ROPE, thick at the base and tapering evenly to a point, its surface finely scaled but CARRYING NO BANDS, NO RINGS AND NO STRIPES of any kind. Coarse shaggy grizzled brown fur, greyish beneath, with large pink feet.
europeanmole: A European mole LYING HORIZONTAL ON ALL FOURS WITH ITS BELLY TOUCHING THE GROUND, its body a smooth low cylinder of dense velvety black-grey fur with no neck and no waist. A pointed pink fleshy snout points forward at the front. Its two front paws are ENORMOUS, BROAD, PINK AND SPADE-SHAPED, held OUT SIDEWAYS AT GROUND LEVEL beside its head with the palms turned outward. It does not stand up, does not rear, and does not hold anything.
grasssnake: A grass snake lying in a loose open curve, a slim olive-green snake with keeled scales, a rounded snout and round pupils. Just behind its head THE SNAKE'S OWN SCALES TURN PALE YELLOW for a short stretch on each side of the neck, and immediately behind that pale area they turn BLACK in a broken crescent. This is a change in the colour of its scales - not a band, not a ring, and not anything worn around its neck. Small dark bars mark its flanks.
plainspocketgopher: A plains pocket gopher on all fours, a stout cylindrical digging rodent with a large flat head, tiny eyes and tiny ears. ITS TWO UPPER FRONT TEETH POINT STRAIGHT FORWARD OUT OF THE FRONT OF ITS FACE, broad, flat and chisel-ended, coloured DEEP ORANGE-YELLOW, projecting horizontally like a pair of small orange blades. They do NOT hang downward and are NOT curved. A fur-lined pouch opens on the outside of each cheek. Heavy curved digging claws, brown fur, short bare tail.
acornbarnacle: An acorn barnacle, a small marine animal built as a SQUAT CIRCULAR WALL OF SIX ROUGH CHALKY OFF-WHITE PLATES fused edge to edge, wider at the base than the top like a tiny crater. ITS ONLY OPENING IS AT THE VERY TOP: a diamond-shaped slot closed by two pairs of moving doors, and A FAN OF FINE CURLED FEATHERY LEGS REACHES OUT OF THAT TOP OPENING AND CURLS UPWARD. The base is sealed flat and nothing protrudes from it.
bluemussel: A blue mussel, a bivalve with a WEDGE-SHAPED SHELL pointed at the hinge end and broadly rounded at the other. Its shell is a DEEP DULL BLUE-BLACK, nearly black along the edges and only faintly blued across the middle, its surface matte to satin rather than mirrored or jewelled, marked with fine concentric growth lines. It gapes slightly, showing a pale cream mantle edge and a bundle of fine tough golden-brown anchoring threads at the pointed end.
bumblebeebat: A bumblebee bat, A BAT, and ITS THIN DARK LEATHERY WINGS ARE THE MOST OBVIOUS THING ABOUT IT: folded closed at its sides with the long finger bones showing as ridges through the membrane. It is astonishingly tiny, about the size and weight of a large bumblebee. Its muzzle is short and swollen with a fleshy nose-pad and wide nostrils, its ears large and rounded with a slender pointed inner flap, its eyes tiny, its fur reddish-brown. It sits upright on small clawed feet.
kangaroorat: A kangaroo rat sitting upright on its haunches, a small sandy-buff rodent with VERY LARGE POWERFUL HIND LEGS and tiny short forepaws held at its chest. Its head is big and blunt with enormous dark eyes and fur-lined cheek pouches. ITS TAIL IS LONG, THIN AND NEARLY BARE ALONG MOST OF ITS LENGTH, ending in a SMALL FLAT TUFT OF LONGER HAIRS ONLY AT THE VERY TIP - a thin rod, never bushy and never furred along its length.
namibdesertbeetle: A Namib desert beetle, A BEETLE WITH SIX LEGS AND A HARD DOMED SHELL: its fused wing cases form a smooth matte-black oval dome covering the whole back, split by a fine straight seam down the middle and covered in a regular pattern of small raised bumps. Its head is small with short elbowed antennae. It stands HEAD-DOWN WITH ITS REAR END TILTED HIGH into the air on six long stilt-like legs.
pistolshrimp: A pistol shrimp, a small shrimp WITH TWO WILDLY MISMATCHED CLAWS, and the difference between them is the entire point. ONE CLAW IS ENORMOUS, as large as the shrimp's whole body, heavy and blocky and held out in front, cocked open with a thick pivoting hammer on its upper jaw. THE OTHER CLAW IS TINY, an ordinary little pincer barely a tenth the size. Its body is semi-transparent, banded orange and white, with short antennae and small stalked eyes.
blueshark: A blue shark in a SIMPLE LEVEL SIDE PROFILE swimming straight, a slender graceful SHARK with a long conical snout ROUNDED AT THE TIP - not a spear, not a bill and not a swordfish. Five gill slits, large dark round eyes. Its pectoral fins are EXTREMELY LONG, NARROW AND CURVED LIKE SCYTHE BLADES, held out level to the sides. Deep indigo blue along the back, brighter blue on the flanks, cut off sharply against a snow-white belly.
loggerheadturtle: A loggerhead sea turtle swimming level in side profile WITH ITS MOUTH CLOSED, a sea turtle whose HEAD IS ENORMOUS AND BLOCKY, far too large for its body, ending in a heavy hooked horny beak with thick jaw muscles bulging at the cheeks. Its heart-shaped shell is reddish-brown and slightly ridged, its neck and flippers warm yellow-brown and scaled in large plates, and each long paddle-shaped front flipper carries a single claw.
oceanicwhitetipshark: An oceanic whitetip shark in a LEVEL SIDE PROFILE, RIGHT WAY UP AND SWIMMING STRAIGHT, a stocky broad-bodied shark with a short bluntly rounded snout. ITS FIRST BACK FIN AND ITS PECTORAL FINS ARE VERY LARGE, BROAD AND ROUNDED AT THE TIPS like paddles, and the rounded tip of each of those fins is MOTTLED WHITE as though dipped in paint. Bronze-grey along the back, pale below.
portuguesemanowar: A Portuguese man o' war, WHICH IS NOT A JELLYFISH AND HAS NO BELL AND NO DOME. Above the water it is a SMOOTH ELONGATED GAS-FILLED FLOAT SHAPED LIKE A LONG POINTED BALLOON LYING HORIZONTALLY, translucent pale blue shading to pink at both ends, and along its entire top edge stands a THIN UPRIGHT RUFFLED CREST like a low sail. Beneath one end hangs a DENSE UNTIDY BUNDLE of bright blue tentacles of wildly unequal length, a few immensely long and fine.
remora: A remora, a slim dark grey fish. THE SUCKING DISC IS PART OF ITS SKULL AND NOT AN OBJECT SITTING ON TOP OF IT: the entire flat upper surface of its head IS the disc, a shallow oval plate flush and continuous with the skin, ridged across with many fine parallel movable slats, running from the snout back past the eyes. Its lower jaw juts forward beyond the upper, and its body tapers to a small forked tail.
sargassumfrogfish: A sargassum frogfish WITH ITS MOUTH CLOSED, a small squat rounded fish mottled olive, gold and white with dark scribbled lines. Its whole body and fins are broken up by many ragged fleshy tassels and weed-like flaps of skin growing directly out of the skin in every direction. Its front fins are ARM-LIKE with an elbow-like joint and splayed finger-like rays, and it props itself up on them. Small eyes, a small upturned mouth held shut.
sootyshearwater: A sooty shearwater in level gliding flight seen from below, a medium seabird UNIFORMLY DARK CHOCOLATE-BROWN, with LONG NARROW STIFF STRAIGHT WINGS held out flat and slightly bowed downward, and a SHORT ROUNDED TAIL. The centre of each underwing carries a BROAD SILVERY-PALE FLASH running along its length. Its bill is long, slim and dark with a hooked tip and raised tubular nostrils along the top.
alpinesalamander: An Alpine salamander STANDING FLAT ON ALL FOURS WITH ITS BELLY CLOSE TO THE GROUND AND ITS BODY HELD HORIZONTAL, a slender amphibian entirely glossy jet-black with no markings, its skin smooth, shining and wet-looking. Its four short legs SPLAY OUT SIDEWAYS from the body, its broad blunt head is level with its spine, and its rounded tail trails straight out behind. A row of deep parallel grooves runs along each flank.
apollobutterfly: An Apollo butterfly with its wings spread flat and open. ITS FRONT PAIR OF WINGS CARRY ONLY BLACK SPOTS AND NO RED AT ALL, on chalky white with thin greyish almost-transparent outer edges. ONLY THE REAR PAIR OF WINGS CARRY RED: on each hindwing sit TWO ROUND SCARLET EYE-SPOTS RINGED IN BLACK, and nowhere else. Its body is small, grey and furry.
barheadedgoose: A bar-headed goose in side view, a pale grey goose with an orange-yellow bill and orange legs. THE MARKING MUST BE CLEARLY VISIBLE ON THE BACK OF ITS HEAD: TWO BOLD DARK BLACKISH-BROWN HORSESHOE-SHAPED BANDS LIE ACROSS THE WHITE CROWN AND NAPE, one behind the other, each curving down toward the eye. The rest of the head is white, and a white stripe runs down each side of the grey neck.
lammergeier: A lammergeier in flight seen from below, a HUGE vulture with LONG NARROW POINTED WINGS and a LONG WEDGE-SHAPED DIAMOND-POINTED TAIL. Its head is FULLY FEATHERED and cream-white with a BLACK BANDIT MASK through the eye, a pale eye ringed in red, and a TUFT OF STIFF BLACK BRISTLES hanging beneath the bill. ITS HEAD, BREAST AND BELLY ARE A STRONG RUSTY ORANGE against dark slate-grey wings.
mountaingoat: A mountain goat standing in side view, a HEAVY THICKSET CLIMBER with a DEEP CHEST, a PRONOUNCED HUMP OF MUSCLE OVER THE SHOULDERS, a SHORT THICK NECK and short sturdy legs - stocky and low-slung, never long-necked and never slender. Its coat is thick shaggy pure white hanging in long chaps over the legs, it has a white beard under the chin, and its horns are SHORT, SLENDER AND JET BLACK, curving gently backward.
rockhyrax: A rock hyrax, a plump ROUNDED animal about the size of a rabbit with NO TAIL AT ALL, standing on four short sturdy legs ending in rubbery padded feet. Its body is a compact oval, its head short and blunt with a small mouth, small rounded ears and long black whiskers. Its fur is dense coarse grey-brown, and a small PALE PATCH SITS IN THE MIDDLE OF ITS BACK ALONG THE SPINE, not on its flank.
woollyflyingsquirrel: A woolly flying squirrel WITH ITS LIMBS STRETCHED OUT SIDEWAYS SO THE GLIDING MEMBRANE IS OPEN AND CLEARLY VISIBLE: a LOOSE FURRED SHEET OF SKIN RUNS ALONG EACH FLANK FROM WRIST TO ANKLE, pulled taut and spread wide like a square of cloth on either side of the body. It is a very large squirrel, the size of a domestic cat, with dense woolly grey-brown fur, very large dark eyes, small rounded ears and a long thick heavily furred tail.
